text:
anya: Quick UX review — I sketched two alternatives for the Model Catalog filter area. One is a 'pills-first' row (compact, shows active filters as pills + count), the other is a collapsible filter rail that can be expanded. Short thread for feedback?

samir: Pills-first looks clean, but worried about horizontal scroll on small screens. Can we collapse overflow into a "+3" menu?

lina: +1 to overflow menu. Also we should surface keyboard access: focus should go to the first pill, then arrow to next. Right now no visible focus ring in the mock. a11y nit.

mike: Implementation note — the pills are easy, overflow menu adds some JS for measurements but doable. Collapsible rail requires layout changes and might break existing compare-table width constraints.

anya: Good call. New idea: pills-first on narrow screens, full rail for large screens. Pills compress to icons + tooltip if >5. Thoughts on microcopy for the tooltips?

lina: Keep tooltips short: e.g., "Reranking: high latency" or "Quantized: lower memory". Avoid model-internal jargon. Also, use aria-label on the pill buttons so screenreaders read state like "Filter: family = mpt, selected".

samir: Related: performance badges — should they live inside the compare table row or above as a per-model badge? I feel inline is more scannable for A/B decisions. But color is tricky for colorblind folks.

lina: Use shape + color. Badge icons (circle/hex) + colorblind-friendly palette and explicit text like "1.2s p50". Also add an accessible tooltip triggered on focus that reads the benchmark context (seq len, batch, hw).

mike: From infra POV, the benchmark context is important but we can't fetch heavy telemetry on every catalog render. Suggest lazy-load detailed tooltip content on hover/focus (aria-live to announce when loaded). Quick inline number comes from cached profile.

anya: Sounds good. Another UX: version pinning. Current proposal is a modal that appears when you click the pin. Some PMs prefer inline pin toggle in the row (fast), designer side prefers modal for commit message + reason. Which is better?

samir: Inline toggle = lower friction. But we need audit trail for Dedicated/Private customers. Maybe inline toggle with a small optional 'Add note' prompt that opens a modal if user wants to annotate. For enterprise users, we can require note.

lina: For keyboard flow, inline toggle should be a button with aria-pressed. Modal opening from 'add note' must trap focus and return focus to the toggle after close. Add confirmation toast copy: "Pinned model v2.1 to route /chat — undo".

mike: Engineering flag: inline pin toggles generate background rollout jobs today. Modal variant would attach metadata to the job. Both okay. Pref server API to accept optional "note" field.

anya: Copy tweak idea: instead of "Pin version" use "Lock model"? Pro: clearer for non-technical users. Con: might imply immutability. Thoughts?

lina: I prefer "Pin version" — industry expected. If we use "Lock" we need to explain differences in a tooltip. Keep label consistent across Console.

samir: UX trade: show small secondary text under model name with current pinned route(s) so teams don't have to open rollout UI. Could be collapsed under a chevron.

anya: Accessibility checklist for this ticket: visible focus states on pills, aria-labels for badges and pins, keyboard path for overflow menu, aria-live for lazy-loaded tooltip data, and color contrast >=4.5 for small text. Lina can you draft quick a11y checklist for the PR?

lina: Yep, I'll add it to the ticket and include examples for contrast ratios and keyboard nav.

design-bot: Created design task: https://figma.redwood/designs/abc123 — comment by anya

mike: I'll scope implementation tasks after Lina posts the checklist. Rough ETA: 2 sprints for pills + overflow + inline pin; tooltip lazy-load in sprint 3.

anya: Thanks all — I'll update the mocks with the overflow + inline pin option and attach to the ticket. :thumbsup:
